_methodology.note: Same schema as the Turkey food dataset for consistency. Madeira's traditional cuisine leans heavily on meat and fish (island economy, historically limited arable land) so the vegetarian/vegan set here is thinner than Turkey's - flagged honestly rather than padded out with dishes that aren't really part of the local repertoire.
_methodology.richness: light | moderate | rich - relative fat/oil/butter/sugar content
_methodology.safeOption: true if spiceLevel is none/mild AND richness is light/moderate
_methodology.images: Use wikipediaTitle with the Wikipedia REST API pattern from the Turkey/activities build. Several niche Madeiran dish pages are thin or non-existent on Wikipedia - worth spot-checking these more than the Turkey set before shipping.

dishes.name: Tomato Salad
dishes.description: Sliced tomato with onion, olive oil and vinegar - a plain, cooling side found at almost any tasca (local eatery).

dishes.name: Vegetable Soup
dishes.description: Blended seasonal vegetable soup, usually pumpkin, carrot and potato-based - mild and filling, often the safest starter on any menu.

dishes.name: Green Beans & Potato
dishes.description: Green beans and boiled potato dressed simply in olive oil - a plain vegetable side, naturally vegan.

dishes.name: Fresh Tropical Fruit Plate
dishes.description: Madeira's volcanic soil and subtropical climate grow passionfruit, custard apple (anona), banana and papaya locally - a genuinely light, unspiced, vegan way to finish a meal instead of dessert.

dishes.name: Grilled Mixed Vegetables
dishes.description: Courgette, pepper and aubergine grilled plain with a little olive oil - common as a side, easy to order without seasoning added.

dishes.name: Cornbread
dishes.description: Dense, slightly sweet cornmeal bread - plain on its own, though often served alongside richer soups or stews.

dishes.name: Skewered Beef
dishes.description: Chunks of beef marinated in garlic and coarse salt, skewered on a laurel branch and grilled over an open fire - Madeira's single most iconic dish, traditionally hung above the table on a metal stand.

dishes.name: Steak Sandwich in Bolo do Caco
dishes.description: A garlic-marinated steak tucked into Madeira's signature griddle-baked flatbread - the island's answer to a steak sandwich, and a popular quick lunch in Funchal.

dishes.name: Wine & Garlic Marinated Pork
dishes.description: Pork marinated for days in wine, garlic and bay leaf before frying - traditionally a Christmas dish, heavy on garlic and richly flavored.

dishes.name: Chicken in a Clay Pot
dishes.description: Chicken slow-cooked in a sealed clay pot with wine, bacon, brandy and tomato - a rich, home-style Portuguese dish found on traditional Madeiran menus.

dishes.name: Madeira Honey Cake
dishes.description: Dense, dark spiced cake made with sugarcane honey, cinnamon, cloves and walnuts - traditionally made once a year for Christmas and kept for months, considered vegetarian (not vegan, due to honey).

dishes.name: Madeira Cheese Tarts
dishes.description: Small tarts of fresh cheese, sugar and cinnamon in a light pastry shell - a regional variation on the Portuguese queijada, sold in Funchal's Mercado dos Lavradores.

dishes.name: Custard Tarts
dishes.description: Flaky pastry cups filled with egg custard, dusted with cinnamon - the national Portuguese classic, available everywhere on the island.

dishes.name: Sweet Bolo do Caco
dishes.description: The same griddle-baked sweet-potato flatbread served with honey and butter instead of garlic - a milder, less rich version than the savory garlic-butter original.

dishes.name: Black Scabbardfish with Banana
dishes.description: Funchal's signature dish - the eel-like black scabbardfish, found almost nowhere else in the world at this depth, pan-fried and served with fried banana. Mild in flavor despite the unusual pairing.

dishes.name: Grilled Limpets
dishes.description: Limpets grilled in their shells with garlic butter and lemon - a common starter along the coast, rich from the butter but mild in spice.

dishes.name: Fried Cornmeal Cubes
dishes.description: Set cornmeal (like a firm polenta) cut into cubes and pan-fried until golden - a traditional side dish, usually served alongside espetada.

dishes.name: Fish Stew
dishes.description: Mixed fish and shellfish stewed with potato, tomato and onion - a lighter, broth-based alternative to the fried fish dishes common elsewhere on the menu.

dishes.name: Garlic Bolo do Caco
dishes.description: Round, flat sweet-potato bread cooked on a hot griddle stone (the 'caco') and split open with garlic butter - Madeira's defining bread, sold everywhere from bakeries to beach bars.

dishes.name: Poncha
dishes.description: Madeira's traditional drink - sugarcane spirit (aguardente) mixed with honey and citrus juice, historically medicinal and now the island's signature cocktail. Not food, but a defining part of eating out here; ask for a lighter pour if wanted.

dishes.name: Grilled Salt Cod
dishes.description: Desalted cod simply grilled and finished with olive oil - the mildest, least greasy of the countless bacalhau preparations found across Portuguese menus (many others are battered and deep-fried).

dishes.name: Garlic Shrimp
dishes.description: Shrimp sizzled in olive oil, garlic and chili in a small clay dish - punchy and rich, usually shared as a starter.

dishes.name: Bread Soup
dishes.description: Bread soaked in garlic-and-coriander broth, usually finished with a poached egg - can be ordered without the seafood version some restaurants add, making it vegetarian.

dishes.name: Wheat & Bean Soup
dishes.description: Hearty wheat-berry and bean soup, traditionally made with meat stock and cabbage - a rustic, mild-flavored dish; ask for a vegetable-stock version if wanted.
